utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Before we start with the proceedings this morning, and I think it's with the cross-examination, I'd just like to say that today we plan to work until 5.00 p.m., and on Wednesday as well. I'd also like to say that in respect of the dimensions of the various rooms, the Chamber would also like to get the height of the rooms. I think we have the length and breadth, we'd also like to get the height as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Witness C, I'd like to ask you some questions first of all, please, about last week. Were you here in The Hague throughout last week?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Did you hear the question, Witness C?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Would you answer it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't know if we're hearing the translation is the problem. I heard the witness answer the first time and then we had the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Mr. Ryneveld, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: I was about to say that I think that the difficulty is that we're not hearing the interpretation coming through the headset. I think the witness did answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Greaves.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: I don't want you to tell us where you were staying, Witness C, but were you staying in a hotel here in The Hague with other people who were due to give evidence or had given evidence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness be advised to move closer to the microphone. That might help.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Witness C, will you move closer to the microphones.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: And in particular, Witness C, did you meet with and speak with people who had already given evidence last week?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Did you speak -- don't tell us any names at all, that's very important -- did you speak with them about the evidence which they had given?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Or anything to do with the case involving the three defendants?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Did you learn if they had been given, as you have been given, pseudonyms for the purpose of giving evidence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: For person B, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: How did you learn that that person had been given a pseudonym if you didn't talk about the case, Witness C?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because the two of us came from Bosnia, and before coming to The Hague, we discussed the matters of witness protection, mostly the protection of our identities because we had come together and we had come from Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: I'd like to move now into closed session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, closed session.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness C, is it correct that in relation to these matters, you have, on two previous occasions, made written statements about events in Prijedor, one in August 1992 -- I'm sorry. I will start that again. One in June 2000 and a second one in August 2000; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: The first of those two that I mentioned in June 2000 is referred to as being a statement made to AID. Will you just explain to us exactly who AID is or are?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what they are involved in, but I know that the official of the SUP, in fact, I thought it was the MUP or the SUP, I thought this man worked there. He called me up and asked me whether I knew – [redacted] [redacted].He called me up and asked me whether I could give a statement on the camp. This is the first time that I gave a statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: In that statement you referred to the people who came to your house as Chetniks, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: And that is a term that is used by people in Bosnia as a term of abuse, isn't it, when referring to those on the other -- perceived to be on the other side who are involved in armed activities, isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what they think, but my view that all those "uniformed" soldiers, uniformed I put in quotation marks, who did not observe the rules of engagements and the rules of service of the military, all those who did not respect such rules, to me, are Chetniks.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Well, the group that came to detain you, did they do anything wrong to you other than to arrest you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, in the house when they arrested me, I was -- they did nothing to me. But later on, when I had to kneel down, when I had to sing these Chetniks' songs, things like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: The phrase "Chetnik", I suggest to you, is of a similar degree of offensiveness as the phrase "balija" would be to a Muslim. That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the most part, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Why didn't you use the phrase Chetnik in your statement to the ICTY then, Witness C?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not pay any attention to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Was it perhaps because you were trying to conceal from the ICTY your true views about the people on the other side?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you now about the takeover the Prijedor, please, if I may. 30th of April 1992, would you accept that that was a bloodless takeover?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Although you've told us that you were prevented from working, is it correct that in general, life continued much as normal apart from the security clampdown in terms of checkpoints?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. It was normal for the Serb people, but not for the others.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Although you were prevented from working, it was by no means universal that everybody was prevented from working, was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: When talking of the checkpoints last week, you spoke about Muslims being stopped, but the checkpoints were stopping everybody and checking up on everybody's identity, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Uniformed men were not checked and, for the most part, all the uniformed men were Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Yes. But what about those Serbs who were not in uniform who wanted to go through checkpoints? What about those? They surely were stopped, were they not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they knew them.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: So the people on the checkpoints knew every Serb in Prijedor so they didn't have to stop them; is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the most part, yes, because these checkpoints were in various neighbourhoods of town so they would know most local residents from that area, Muslim and Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: And if a Serb came from another part of town and visited another suburb, the people on the checkpoints there, they would know them automatically, would they? Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. His documents would probably be checked if they didn't wear a uniform, but for the most part they did wear a uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: The end of May, Witness C, it's right, isn't it, that there was some fighting in the Prijedor area; do you accept that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: And there was fighting between Serb forces and Muslim and Croat forces; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: And it was in reaction to that that the first large number of arrests and detentions took place; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: The site of Keraterm, would you accept this proposition, Witness C, that the site itself, on two sides at least, was open to two major public roads? Do you accept that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: And anybody passing in a vehicle or on foot or on a bicycle could see into the main -- main area of the compound? Would you accept that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: The fence that surrounded the compound was just an ordinary industrial piece of fencing, not particularly tall, no barbed wire or anything like that around it; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not in Keraterm.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Sorry, it may be that your answer has come out slightly confused. Let me just make it absolutely plain. There was no barbed wire around the fence; is that what you're accepting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: The date of your arrest was the 12th of June, 1992, and the first time that you saw the man you've identified as Dusko Sikirica was around two weeks or a bit more than two weeks later, the 27th of June; would that be about right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Before that I saw him in a car, but after that, I would see him up close.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Would Your Honour just give me a moment, please? Would Your Honour just give me a moment, please? I'm sorry. I've lost my note. I'll come back to that in a moment, if I may.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: You were interrogated at Keraterm. How soon after your arrival there was the interrogation conducted?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately after 20 to 25 days, maybe 20.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: And what was the nature of the questions which you were asked?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same as before, whether before the war I had been politically active, whether I had been a member of the SDA party, what was I doing, what was I involved in, things like that. What my brothers were doing, things like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: After the interrogation -- the people who conducted it, they were known as inspectors; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Interrogators, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: And was it they who decided on what was to happen to individual detainees, where they would be taken?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: The inspectors or interrogators, they would come from outside every day; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: The number of prisoners who were in the camp whilst you were there, could you give us a number for that, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Let's say approximately 500 to 600 men, when I arrived, but later, the number increased significantly.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: To what sort of figure, Witness C?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is hard to say exactly but I think approximately to -- up to 1200 to 1400 men, somewhere around there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: When you first arrived, it's right, isn't it, that a man called Knezevic was the commander of the camp; do you accept that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very briefly, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: When you say "very briefly," what do you mean by "very briefly"? How long was he commander for?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: About ten days, somewhere around there. Perhaps less, seven to ten days.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: And was his first name Zivko Knezevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that I had stated so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: And before the war, you knew of him, is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in a way.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Is this right, that he had been in the police, had retired, and had subsequently been recalled to service?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Is this also right, Witness C, and it may be that you've gathered this information from your inquiries about events in Prijedor, that a second police station was established in Prijedor at the time of the takeover of the municipality?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: If Your Honour will just give me a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: In an area of Prijedor called Urije Dva, I hope I've pronounced that correctly, does that refresh your memory?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I could not move about so that I really had very little information. I don't know. Blank pages inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Blank pages inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. 25

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Did you, yourself, see this man Zivko Knezevic in Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: A few times, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Was that only when he was said to be the commander or throughout your stay at Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only when he was the commander. It was only then that I saw him a few times.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: The ratio of guards to prisoners when the population of detainees was at its height, would that have been approximately 15 guards to some 1.500 or 1.400 detainees? Would you accept that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: By and large, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Throughout your period of detention at Keraterm, Witness C, is this correct that had the authorities so chosen, they could, at any time, have killed all of you?

utterances.speaker: MS. BALY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I object to the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. On what ground?

utterances.speaker: MS. BALY
utterances.text: It calls for, in my submission, speculation on the part of the witness. It's not for him to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Suppose it was rephrased: "Was there anything to prevent the killing of all the detainees?" Could you object to that question?

utterances.speaker: MS. BALY
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, I couldn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: I'm grateful for Your Honour's assistance, as always.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Witness C, was there anything which existed to prevent the killing of all the detainees by those who -- in whose power you were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you repeat the question, please? I don't understand it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Was there anything to prevent all the detainees from being killed if those in whose power you were had so chosen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not only that, they could also decide not to kill anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Just a little, please, about the conditions which existed at the -- at Keraterm. Were you, on occasions, permitted to have exercise outside the buildings?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Was that on a daily basis?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Every other day, every third day; how often, Witness C?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: It depended on the shift leader and the mood they were in.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: The three different shifts which we've heard about in evidence, would this be right that no two shifts had the same routine of operating?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: And by "routine", I mean the times at which meals would be taken, the times at which doors would be opened. All those things were different depending on which shift, who was running the shift at any particular time; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is, on the shift leader and other guards in case the shift leader was absent.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: The date when you left Keraterm would be the 3rd or 4th or perhaps later in August 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: That or maybe 5th August. I'm not quite sure. I don't remember well, but it must have been either August 3rd or the 5th.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: And about a week or so before you left Keraterm, it's right, isn't it, that a new commander came to the camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the massacre in number three, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: And his name was Marinko Sadzak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't know. I know he was quite elderly.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: I'd like to turn now about the allegation you make against Mr. Sikirica of a killing. The first thing I'd like you to do, so that we may know who it is, would you be so kind as to write down on a piece of paper the name of your best man, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Witness writes].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What is to be done with this?

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: I think in the first instance it should be shown to Your Honours, as a matter of courtesy, if nothing else, and then if I could see it, please, and then we can have it exhibited. Thank you very much. I think other counsel ought to see that as well, I think, properly. And I'm gently reminded by Mr. Ryneveld that he'd like to have a look.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Your Honour, perhaps that better become an exhibit, please, and it's obviously one that, because it involves potential identification, ought to be a closed exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. What's the number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Defence Exhibit D1/1.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Again, Witness C, without doing anything which is capable of identifying that person by name, is it right that your best man, whose name you've just written down for us, he was of Serb ethnicity; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: The place where you say the murder took place, that spot would be in full view, would it not, of both the main road and the road to the entrance of Keraterm? Do you accept that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the main road, yes, but not from the main gate.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: As far as the evidence that you gave concerning that allegation, Witness C, you told Their Honours last week that it was an inmate who had told you to go to the gate; do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. A guard came and told me that I had a visitor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: So why did you tell Their Honours last week that it was an inmate who had summoned you to the gate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not an inmate, a guard only, because a guard came to the dormitory and asks for so and so, so of course it's possible that detainees, since we know one another, they will then look for that man, is he in this room or in Room 2 or 3, so that is perhaps how it should be interpreted, because detainees were not allowed to come close to the camp entrance, no way.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: You told Their Honours last week that as you walked along the asphalt path back to the buildings, you looked sideways and saw the inmate. You believed him to be kneeling in front of Sikirica. Was Sikirica standing at that point, Witness C?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Why, then, when you made your statement to AID, did you say that you saw Sikirica sitting on a patch of grass to the right with the prisoner?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never said that. I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Well, we have a translation of the statement that you made and it quite clearly says in that statement that you saw Sikirica sitting. Any explanation at all for that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Well, I have no doubt we can check the original that was made and see whether that's correct. When you gave evidence about having heard the shot and turning to look in the direction of the shot, you told Their Honours that you saw Sikirica putting the pistol back in a holster behind his belt. Why did you tell the Bosnian authorities in that statement that you saw Sikirica holding the pistol and pointing at the prisoner who lay dead? Those two things are different, aren't they, Witness C?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, returning the pistol, at that split second when I looked up, it could mean both things, returning, because I wasn't really watching. It simply -- when I heard the shot it was a matter of a split second. I just turned, had a look and fled, so that -- it was a split second, so that --

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: In evidence last week, you said that you heard Sikirica saying or shouting, "This is how every inmate who tries to escape will fare. I shall personally settle the score with him." Do you remember telling us that last week?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely, precisely, to a word.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Why, then, did you tell not just AID but also the OTP that what Sikirica said at that point was, "Fuck your mother, that's what will happen to anybody who tries to escape from this camp," or the slightly alternative version to the OTP, "Fuck your mothers, this is what will happen to all of you who attempt to escape from the camp. I will personally deal with them." Why did you say that in your statements?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the oath, the expletive was in plural.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: You were the only person who witnessed this incident, weren't you, Witness C?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: You were the only person in the area, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, well, the nearest, maybe the nearest, yes, but other detainees could see that too.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: What I suggest to you, Witness C, is that the variations in the story that you have told to different people is explained by the fact that it didn't happen, did it? There was no such incident.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what you think.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Did you hear the name of the alleged victim, the pilot, at any stage?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not, or I may have but I do not remember it. What I do know well is that the detainees in Room 2 said that he was a pilot, and that he was mentally unstable. That he wandered around the camp without any control so that he wasn't the man who had ever tried to escape.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: If I was to put to you the name Bajazit Jakupovic, would that refresh your memory about the man's name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I wouldn't know, really.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: You were aware of, in any event, this pilot whose -- had lost his mind who was in Keraterm at one stage?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, afterwards. After he was killed. It was then that we had talked about who he was, what he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: You see, I suggest that that person wasn't killed at that stage and he was, in fact, transferred to Omarska where he was killed.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what you think.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: You were just subjected to one beating; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, except they tried to do it a second time but it was only God Almighty who saved me then. So they tried to do it twice, twice, and I survived by chance.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Upon your arrival, you weren't beaten, I think, because you had money; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. At first I thought that that was the reason, not I, but my neighbour, because he told me later on that he had had some money with him. But then I was told that it was because Kole was the shift leader and they did not beat people on that shift.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Having been put into Room 2, you were detained there for a total of about a month; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, less, I think. I transferred after about ten days to Room 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: You see what you told the Bosnian authorities in the statement made to them was that, "They put us in hall 2 which is where they put the non-Serbs from Donja Puharska who'd been arrested on the 30th of May and taken from their homes to the camp. We were there for about a month." Do you recall telling the Bosnian authorities that in your statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly. Listen, when one considers some details in greater length, then it is quite possible that there is an inconsistency, because at the investigation documentation agency, the AID, in Bosnia, never paid a -- they simply did not pay attention and I just talked. Besides, I wasn't really prepared for it, because until that time I simply did not pause to think about the camp, about all this horror. And it is very difficult to recall it and talk about it. So that the whole statement was an ad hoc statement. So it shouldn't come as a surprise to you that it is not precise. It was only afterwards when I heard from The Hague that I should come here then, I guess, on my own, well, I began to think about those things in some detail. Even for two or three days when I come home and then start analysing these things, and then I realise that I should have been more precise in my statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: During the period that you were in Room 2, nobody was mistreated, were they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The first night people were taken out and killed. I can give you the name of my friend, my friend who was beaten up that first night.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Just returning briefly to the issue of the pilot, was the man you've identified as a pilot, was he the only one, only pilot who was in Keraterm, as far as you knew?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. That is what I heard. I did not know him. I wasn't in the same dormitory with him. It was after the camp, afterwards I heard that he was a pilot. I did not know him at all. I simply did not pay much attention to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Did you ever hear later that other pilots had been detained at Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, I didn't pay any attention to it, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: The people who were detained in Room 1, you observed at one -- at some stage that nobody was taken out from Room 1 and beaten, were they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't say no one. Let me see how to put it. In comparison with number 2, it was a negligible -- it was much better, much easier in Room 1 because it contained interrogated detainees from Puharska.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Well, Witness C, forgive me, but what you told the Bosnian authorities was that when you were, "... transferred to hall 1 amongst already questioned inmates, because I had noticed that no one from number 1 was taken out and beaten." So the position is, I suggest to you, that nobody from Room 1 was taken out and beaten?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was taken from Room 1 and beaten, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: What happened after your release, Witness C, did you go back to your home?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: How long did you remain there for?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: About two months, maybe two months and a half.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Don't tell us where you went to, but did you then leave the Prijedor area completely?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: During the two months between your release and your departure from the Prijedor area, is this correct,that you could have been re-arrested at any time by the authorities?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: And again during that period, there would have been nothing to prevent the authorities from killing you at that stage; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: That I couldn't say. That is a vague question.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Petrovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Witness C, how long have you known Kajin?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not know him at all. Perhaps just from sight in town.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: How frequently would you see him in town? And I'm referring to the period before the war.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very few times, perhaps a couple of times. His brother, yes, but Kajin himself, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Where would you have seen him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, in passing, in town.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: If I understood you correctly, you know his brother better?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: How do you know him? If I can just ask you to slow down and wait until my questions are translated to you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: From town, really.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: What is his name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Does he have any nickname?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: In your statement, you said that you did not see Kajin committing any crime in Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Personally I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you have any contact with him while you were in Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: No direct contact with him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: With his brother?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps we saw each other once.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: When did you see him? How did -- what happened on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, somehow in passing. One was glad to see someone whom one knew.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did he tell you anything?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Could you perhaps remember where you saw him in relation to the room where you were staying?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps on the asphalt walkway in front of number 2, outside.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: In other words, you were outside in front of the room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Correct me if I'm wrong, but you spent 55 days in Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: From what you could have seen, what was the behaviour of Kajin towards those people who were detained there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Personally?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: I'm referring to him personally.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not badly, not badly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: What does that mean, "not badly"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he was correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: When -- during his shift did he allow people to come out of the room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did anyone in his presence limit you in terms of the time that you were given to finish your meals?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Who was this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that the Banovics were in that shift, and they did it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: I was asking in his presence, when he was there.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: In his presence, no, or if -- or perhaps very infrequently.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So if you say "very infrequently," you remember an occasion or do you -- or so? How did it look?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps there could have been a situation when, due to the presence of interrogators, we may have been limited, or if something had happened, some incident, then they wouldn't let us come out in any shift. utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Do you recall such a situation or are you just inferring that on the basis of everything that took place in Keraterm and everything that you knew about Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I infer because I don't have any specific recollection. How could I?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: I assume that that also refers to the going to the toilet?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, overall movement.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Do you recall whether Kajin personally ever limited any of these rights that you had, if I can call it that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, depending on the interrogators up there or if the camp commander would come, then it -- we would be pushed back into the rooms.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: What was Kajin's brother's attitude in the camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw him very infrequently but his behaviour was all right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Let me take you back to the period before the Keraterm. In Donje Puharska a Crisis Staff was established; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether on the 21 November, 1991, a Crisis Staff was established?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I was not politically active and did not take interest in those things.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Do you know who Mirza Mujetic is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Who is it? Could you tell us a little something about him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what I know, he was the SDA president in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Until when did the Prijedor municipal assembly function?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Perhaps until early 1992, but I wouldn't be able to tell you exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Why did it stop functioning? What happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I was not interested in politics at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned, both today and in Thursday, about checkpoints set up by the authorities after the takeover. Do you know anything about any Muslim checkpoints in Hambarine, in Kozaruse?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I may have heard of that, the one in Hambarine, but overall, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And who manned the checkpoint at Hambarine?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that there was an incident there. This is how we in Prijedor learned about it. There was some confrontation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: But who manned the roadblock at Hambarine?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because it's a Muslim village, I suppose it was the Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Do you know how this barricade was operating?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, because I wasn't passing there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us regarding the attack on the town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: For about a month the situation in town was quiet and there were no casualties.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Who took an offensive action against the town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: In your statement you said that in early 1992 the authorities had issued a threat to people, that if they didn't go to Croatia, that they would lose their jobs. Who was the authority in town in this period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that at that time, it was the national parties that had the power.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Which national power -- national parties? We know, but if you can help us with it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was the SDA and I think it was party of the SDS and the HDZ.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So you're referring to all three national parties?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Something like that, at least formally.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Who at that time was the president of the Prijedor municipality?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was Professor Muhamed Cehajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: What party did he represent?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: SDA.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: At that time, if you say that you did not engage in politics and you did not know at the time, but if you know, I would like to know your opinion about the JNA. Whose army was that? Were officers and soldiers coming from all ethnic groups in the country?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: What period are you referring to, early 1992?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, early 1992.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that at that time, in addition to the Serbs, there were other ethnic groups represented there but this was gradually dissipating. In other words, people were leaving it as the war in Croatia progressed. I think that they were leaving it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Who was leaving it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not the Serbs. Muslims and Croats, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: In the town of Prijedor, were there any protests against the Yugoslav Peoples' Army? I'm still referring to the period before the war.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Let me take you back to the period after the takeover of power as you described it. You mentioned that people of non-Serb ethnic background were being taken -- had been taken away their healthcare benefits. Were people of Muslim background receiving any healthcare in healthcare institutions in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I guess there were such cases, but they had to pay for it out of their own pockets.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that, in fact, only in surgery, there were 720 non-Serbs received healthcare based on the health insurance from before the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that. I know that some of the inmates were taken there for medical care.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: You said that they had to pay -- that people had to pay out of their own pockets. If I can extend this, were they also required to pay?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Why don't you ask them?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: When -- did all these troubles start after the takeover of power or even before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the takeover of power, but there were tensions even before. In March you could clearly feel that something was wrong, but especially after the takeover of power.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Now I'm talking about bans and the things like that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it started in March but after the takeover of power, terrible propaganda on radio started and also in Kozarski Vijesnik, the newspaper.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: What was your last date of work in your place of employment, approximately if you can put a date on it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall, trust me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: At least a month?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Early in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: You last went to work in early 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And the reason was what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time it became a rule that only those who were in uniform could enter the perimeter of the company. In other words, only those who had stayed loyal, only those who had stayed loyal to the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: That was in early 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Do you know who was in the management of the largest companies in the Prijedor area at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Who were those?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Balaban, Marijanovic, Cehajic and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Who was the chief of SUP at that time in Prijedor? I'm again referring to early 1992 when you were already not permitted to enter the premises of the company?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was not official, but there were already pressures, and it was an unwritten rule, "Do not show up without uniform." And after the takeover of power, there were actual rules imposed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Before the takeover of power, who was the chief of SUP in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that he was an ethnic Muslim, last name Talundzic or something. I know that he used to work for the [redacted]company, in my company.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: You also mentioned your brothers. Until what time did they stay in their jobs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Same as I did, because at that time,we were some kind of[redacted] there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I ask if we could move to private session briefly, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Let me take you back to the incident at Hambarine again. Do you know who the first casualties of the armed conflict were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what we could learn in Puharska, because that was on the opposite end of the municipality, I think that there was a confrontation between these people, the policemen at the checkpoint and soldiers who were going in the direction of Ljubija.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: My question was: Who were the first casualties?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that there were some on both sides.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: What is the name of the neighbour who ordered you and your brother to come out of the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Brane Bosnjak.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: What is his ethnic background?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I think he's a Serb. At least he referred to himself as a Serb, and his children.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: This armed group, if I can name it that, that arrested you, according to you, to which military structure did they belong? What were they, police, army, White Eagles, paramilitaries?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were all soldiers, at least based on their uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: But according to you, to whom -- to which unit did they belong?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, but they took us to the MUP so they were the legal JNA military. Had they been paramilitaries, I think that they would have taken us somewhere else.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: If they were the military, I don't see the logic of their taking you to the MUP.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: They all worked together.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, do you think that this would be the right moment to take a break, or shall I move on with my questioning?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. This is a convenient time for us to take the break. We will take the break and resume at 11.30. Witness C, you are reminded not to discuss your evidence with anybody, including the Prosecution team.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You may continue, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: When, precisely, do you think that you were arrested unlawfully?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: 12 of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Sorry, I didn't hear you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 12th of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: No, I mean the precise moment when those men came to your house or what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At the moment when my house was surrounded and when I was arrested.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned some persons in the police building in Prijedor; which policemen did you see there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not know those men except that lad while I was kneeling who came to me and asked me what my name was. I knew that young man by sight. I don't know his name. And he told me then to stand up.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Your brother was beaten at the police, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what they told me. As they took him upstairs for interrogation of sorts, it was then that they beat him.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And who beat him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: The man upstairs. That man, what shall I call him, an investigator.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: What was his name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C:  [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned that when you were taken to Keraterm, that some papers were put at the weigh hut. You couldn't see those papers, I understand, but what do you think those papers were?
